speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext:
The question is on motion No. 2, standing in the name of the hon. member for Vegreville (Mr. Mazankowski).
When this bill was called yesterday, Mr. Speaker had some reservations about this motion. I have had the occasion to look at his remarks in Hansard of yesterday and I, too, have reservations. Hon. members may want to assist the Chair in this regard, but it seems to me that there are financial implications in the amendment. If the bill were amended as proposed, and enacted into law, it would put an additional burden on the Treasury. However, what is probably more to the point, and my second concern, is that the proposed motion in the name of the hon. member for Vegreville amends section 17 of the Act which is not a section in the bill and is not before the House at this time. However, I would appreciate hearing the opinions of hon. members if they would like to comment.

subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, I would like to comment briefly on this motion. Under the provisions of section 23 of the Farm Credit Act, the Governor in Council has the power to establish interest rates. He can prescribe rates at 2 per cent, 3 per cent, 4 per cent or 5 per cent. So, I believe that it is within the realm of the provisions of the act.
My second point is that the powers of the Farm Credit Corporation are indeed being expanded to enable it to administer a program for which something in the order of

$150 million is to be appropriated over the next seven years. I believe that in the estimates in excess of $20 million has been appropriated under Votes 1 and 15. This particular program provides for the expenditure of these funds over the next seven years, as I pointed out. Funds are allocated under the program for grants to farmers who wish to retire or leave the business of farming. There are special facilities to be provided and there is the buying and selling of lands, all of which will be a burden on the Treasury, and all of which is provided for under the small farms development program. Delegation of powers is extended under clause 1 of Bill C-5.
I simply ask in this amendment that a certain portion of the funds be allocated for the subsidization of interest rates, because if this is truly a small farms development program it is certainly necessary to provide encouragement and incentive to young farmers to engage in the business of farming. There are other sections of Bill C-5 which refer directly to the administration of the small farms development program, and since such broad powers are granted, I believe that a certain portion of the funds allotted should be provided for the subsidization of interest rates to farmers under the age of 30 who are applying for loans for the first time. I believe that this would certainly give young farmers in Canada a fighting chance to engage in the business of farming, and it would certainly assist them in assembling the kind of viable unit that is necessary to conduct a successful operation.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext: I should like to indicate, if the minister will excuse me for a moment, that I wanted to hear the hon. member for Vegreville who put forward the motion, but I do suggest that he may have diverged from the question of the procedural acceptibility of the motion. I mention this because I see several other hon. members rising. Until we decide on the question of whether or not the Chair can accept the motion, hon. members should direct their comments to the procedural argument.

subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, in speaking directly on the procedural matter, may I point out that this bill does not provide money or in fact make an appropriation for any subsidization of interest rates. Of course, the hon. member defeated his own argument when he admitted that that was the objective of his amendment because, quite obviously, if there is to be a subsidization of interest rates for the purposes described in the amendment it would require a recommendation. Of course, there are rules regarding any motion brought to the House for an appropriation of money or an additional charge on the Treasury, and it is not within the competence of a private member to make such a motion. Of course, he has other methods of bringing that before the House if he chooses.
The other important point is the one to which you alluded, Mr. Speaker, and that is that this amendment does not in fact amend the bill which is before the House today; it attempts to amend the Farm Credit Act. I do not have all the citations before me, but I am sure you are familiar with them, Mr. Speaker. There are dozens of cases where attempts have been made to amend an act sections of which are not contained in the bill before the House. Of course, there is no question that the Farm Credit Act, as contained in Bill C-5, deals with section 17. The other part of the procedural prohibition against a private member
June 28, 1972

moving a motion that is in fact a direct or indirect charge on the Treasury is valid, and this amendment is out of order on both counts.

subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext:
Mr. Speaker, I was not too impressed with the hon. minister's remarks. Bill C-5 amends the Farm Credit Act, and the corporation does lend money at a prescribed interest rate that is 11 per cent higher than the rate at which the government borrows. In this amendment, the hon. member for Vegreville (Mr. Mazankowski) specifies that the interest should be less for a certain portion of the loan. This does not necessarily cause an expenditure of money. I notice that the President of the Treasury Board (Mr. Drury) is nodding his head in agreement with that statement, Mr. Speaker. If the government borrowing rate were to dip, this amendment would not cost the government a cent. Indeed, the Minister of Agriculture (Mr. Olson) told us not so long ago that government interest rates were coming down, so in the near future they may even be below this suggested rate. Indeed, if I took the assurance of the minister to heart I would assume that they are nearly below it now.
The fact is that this amendment may not cost the government any money at all, and it is specified that it should only be made to a farmer of less than 30 years of age, so the government may be saving some money. The bill deals with the Farm Credit Corporation which lends money at an interest rate which may well be below this because it is an adjustable interest rate, not a pegged rate. This amendment cannot be ruled out of order, because it may not cost the government any money at all.

subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext: Mr. Speaker, I wish to concur in the remarks made by the hon. member for Vegreville (Mr. Mazankowski) and the hon. member for Crowfoot (Mr. Horner). This amendment may not cost the government any money at all. I think this procedural difficulty could be solved if the Minister of Agriculture (Mr. Olson) were to accept the amendment.

subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext: Move the amendment, Bud.

subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
subsubtopic: AMENDMENTS RESPECTING LOANS AND POWERS AND CAPITAL OF CORPORATION
speechtext:
Order, please. The Chair has for consideration and decision whether motion No. 2 standing in the name of the hon. member for Vegreville (Mr. Mazankowski) can be accepted by the Chair as being procedurally correct. In my initial remarks, I indicated that I had two concerns. One was that the proposed amendment, if it were enacted, might cause a charge against the Treasury and there is no recommendation accompanying the motion. The second was that it appears to go behing the bill and purports to amend the Farm Credit Act.
The hon. member for Vegreville, the hon. member for Crowfoot and the hon. member for Assiniboia (Mr. Knight) have argued, with respect to the first point, that there will not necessarily be a charge against the Treasury. I would like to look at that argument if I were to base my ruling upon it but, in any event, I would want to base my ruling on the second point which, I indicated earlier, was a bar to the acceptance of this motion. The
Division
motion does not in fact purport to amend the act and, as the Minister of Agriculture (Mr. Olson) has pointed out, the authorities are clear that this is not acceptable from a procedural standpoint. I must, therefore, decline the motion on this basis.
I understand that on Motion No. 1, the yeas and nays have been taken.
Call in the members.
